title: A simple and rapid method for toxicity evaluation of zinc oxide nanoparticle (ZnO NPs) in benthic animal Hydra magnipapillata
author: Yamindago, Lee, et al.

steps.title: Prepare Hydra culture solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1 mM NaCl, 1 mM CaCl₂, 0.1 mM KCl, 0.1 mM MgSO₄, and 1 mM Tris‑[hydroxymethyl]‑aminoethane (pH 7.6) in 20 L of water; this is the Hydra culture solution.

steps.title: Culture Hydra polyps
steps.instruction: Place Hydra magnipapillata wild‑type strain 105 polyps in a cylindrical culture dish (1 L) containing 500 mL of the prepared culture solution; incubate at 18 ± 1 °C with a 12 h dark/12 h light photoperiod. Change the solution daily, six hours after feeding.

steps.title: Prepare fresh Artemia nauplii
steps.instruction: Add Artemia eggs to 1800 mL natural seawater in a 2000 mL jar, aerate, and keep at 25 ± 1 °C. After 48 h harvest the nauplii and rinse twice with Hydra culture solution before feeding the polyps.

steps.title: Starve Hydra polyps
steps.instruction: Remove food and keep the cultured polyps in fresh Hydra culture solution for 48 h before any toxicity assay.

steps.title: Acute toxicity assay (LC50)
steps.instruction: Transfer 10 polyps into each cell‑culture dish, add 10 mL Hydra culture solution containing one of the following ZnO nanoparticle concentrations (spherical, Ø 20 nm): 10, 25, 50, 100, 150, 200, or 300 µg/mL. Include a control dish with no ZnO NPs. Incubate at 18 ± 1 °C for 24, 48, 72, or 96 h without feeding. After each time point, count lethal polyps based on morphology (living normal, tentacle‑clubbed/contracted, or dead) and repeat the experiment three times.

steps.title: Morphological response assay
steps.instruction: Place 10 polyps per dish and add 10 mL Hydra culture solution containing 50 µg/mL ZnO NPs (the 48 h LC₅₀). Include a control dish without NPs. Incubate at 18 ± 1 °C and record morphological changes at 3, 6, 12, and 24 h using a dissecting microscope. Do not feed the polyps. Repeat three times.

steps.title: Regeneration assay
steps.instruction: Decapitate the head of 10 polyps per dish, then add 10 mL Hydra culture solution with 10 µg/mL ZnO NPs; include a control group of decapitated polyps in solution without NPs. Incubate at 18 ± 1 °C and observe regeneration at 24, 48, 72, and 96 h, noting tentacle development and abnormalities. After exposure, transfer any surviving polyps to fresh culture solution without NPs to allow further regeneration. Repeat three times.

steps.title: Analyze mortality data
steps.instruction: Enter the numbers of lethal polyps from the acute toxicity assay into a Probit analysis program to calculate LC₅₀ values with 95 % confidence limits as shown in Table 1.

description: The method presented here provides a simple procedure to determine the lethal concentration and rapid procedures to detect toxic effects of ZnO NPs in morphology and regeneration of H. magnipapillata using morphological characters. This method is used to evaluate the acute toxic impacts of ZnO NPs on H. magnipapillata [1]. This animal is commonly used as an animal model for biological studies and environmental toxicity tests [2]. It can be cultured in controlled laboratory condition with a simple method previously described [3]. The responses of hydra after exposure to ZnO NPs are specific compared to other nanoparticles (e.g., silicon oxide nanoparticles) [4]. This method suggests the reasonable concentration and the exposure time for investigating the toxic effects of ZnO NPs and other nanoparticles in H. magnipapillata. This method will provide important clues for further investigations on the cellular and molecular responses of the animal after exposure to nanoparticles.
